about.free: Play the computer, play a friend online or on one device, and learn the rules with lessons.
about.whatBody: Chess is played on eight ranks and eight files by two armies of sixteen pieces. White moves first. Each piece moves its own way — the queen anywhere in a line, the knight in its L, the pawn straight ahead but capturing across — and the game ends when a king is attacked and cannot get out of it. Three moves are special: castling, where the king and a rook move together; the capture in passing, where a pawn takes another that has just stepped two squares; and promotion, where a pawn that reaches the far side becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight. A game can also end in a draw: stalemate, too little material to mate, the same position three times, or fifty moves without a capture or a pawn move.

rules.title: How to play
rules.intro: Card Chess is chess with a hand of cards. Each turn you play one card, then make a chess move that card allows.
rules.match: Play a card that matches the top of the pile by colour or by number or symbol — the law of Uno. A wild goes on anything.
rules.colors: The card's colour picks who moves: red = queen or rooks, blue = bishops, green = knights, yellow = pawns.
rules.king: The king may move with any card, and castling counts as a king move.
rules.stuck: No card fits? Draw one. Still stuck? Pass — but never while in check: then keep drawing until a card saves your king.
rules.capture: Every capture makes the other player draw a card.
rules.uno: Down to two cards? Tap UNO! before you play, or draw two.
rules.win: Win by checkmate — or by playing your last card.

action.reverse: Reverse: with two players it works like a Skip.
action.draw2: Draw Two: move, your opponent draws two, and you move again.
action.wild: Wild: move any piece, then name the next colour.
action.wild4: Wild Draw Four: as a Wild, and your opponent draws four. Only when you hold no card of the current colour. If any move gives check, the extra move is cancelled.
